# S1TBX / Microwave Toolbox Upgrade Review

## Purpose

This document captures the working model for reviewing ALUs against the legacy S1TBX codebase and the current SNAP Microwave Toolbox. It is intended to support upgrade prioritisation for the restored ALUs fork, with a focus on processing quality rather than cosmetic refactoring or API churn.

In the task wording, references to `s1tbx` should be interpreted in the current SNAP context as the Microwave Toolbox successor repository. The archived `s1tbx` repository remains useful as a provenance and naming reference, but the latest benchmark and upgrade target is `microwave-toolbox`.

## Task Definition

The restored ALUs fork performance will be compared to s1tbx benchmarks that are based on the latest available version. A review of the changes introduced to s1tbx relative to the original version of s1tbx on which ALUs was based is required, with a focus on identifying essential logical changes that affect processing quality and which would need to be addressed in further ALUs fork upgrades. A review of these issues will need to be discussed with JRC.D5 in order to prioritize such upgrades, either in the context of this FBE contract or in follow up activities.

## Provenance Model

ALUs is best treated as a partial native port of selected SNAP/S1TBX processing chains. It contains both operator implementations and a reduced SNAP/S1TBX support layer.

| `algs/backgeocoding` | `s1tbx-op-sentinel1/BackGeocodingOp.java` | `sar-op-sentinel1/BackGeocodingOp.java` | SLC coregistration and coherence chain quality |

## Upstream Rename Model

The active Microwave Toolbox repository preserves the S1TBX git history. Important rename markers in the Microwave Toolbox history are:

| Commit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `9aca04cc5` | Rename from `s1tbx-*` modules to `sar-*` / Microwave Toolbox structure |
| `450907298` | Move Java packages from `org.esa.s1tbx.*` to `eu.esa.sar.*` |

This allows review work to follow Java file history across the rename boundary instead of treating Microwave Toolbox as an unrelated project.

## Review Objective

The review should not attempt to port every upstream change. The objective is to identify upstream logical changes in Microwave Toolbox, relative to the S1TBX-era logic represented in ALUs, that can affect output quality, supported input coverage, or benchmark comparability.

| Change type | Include in review | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Numerical algorithm changes | Yes | Can change calibration, coherence, geolocation, or coregistration outputs |
| Metadata interpretation changes | Yes | Can change input parsing, burst boundaries, orbit timing, no-data semantics, band naming |
| Mission/product support changes | Yes | Required for S1C/S1D, updated SAFE formats, GRD/SLC variants, ETAD-related products |
| Default parameter changes | Yes | Can affect benchmark comparability even if algorithms are unchanged |
| Performance-only changes | Case by case | Relevant only if they alter numerical behavior, tile boundaries, caching semantics, or memory precision |
| Package rename/import cleanup | No | Not relevant unless coupled with logic changes |
| UI-only changes | No | Not relevant for ALUs command-line processing unless defaults or graph parameters changed |

## Initial Drift Areas

These are candidate quality-affecting areas seen from local repository inspection and upstream release notes/history. They require detailed review before any upgrade decision.

| Area | Current observation                                                                                                                                                        | ALUs impact hypothesis |
|---|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---|
| Sentinel-1C and Sentinel-1D | ALUs supports these by default                                                                                                                                             | Developer review note: ALUs already supports this through generic `SENTINEL-1` mission handling rather than an A/B-only whitelist. Public development notes record an S1D IW SLC coherence run with `alus-coh` using `S1D_IW_SLC__1SDV_20260614T152007_20260614T152033_003234_005A51_C931.SAFE` and `S1D_IW_SLC__1SDV_20260626T152007_20260626T152034_003409_00600E_0BC5.SAFE`; keep this entry under review to confirm whether any remaining reader or metadata drift affects S1C/S1D products |
| Sentinel-1 reader | Current `sar-io` has substantial changes including S1 reader performance, caching, updated product handling, OCN/WV updates, COG/GSLC-related work                         | ALUs native reader may miss updated SAFE metadata behavior or product variants relevant to latest benchmarks |
| Thermal noise removal | Current history includes updates after ALUs implementation, including range noise vector selection and SNAP-4160 thermal noise updates                                     | ALUs TNR is quality-critical before calibration and may need targeted logic diffing against current `Sentinel1RemoveThermalNoiseOp` |
| Calibration | Current `Sentinel1Calibrator` includes later support and cleanup, including S1C/S1D and calibration review changes                                                         | ALUs calibration LUT selection, no-data/floor handling, and complex/intensity behavior need comparison against current upstream |
| Backgeocoding | Current `BackGeocodingOp` has extensive post-S1TBX changes, including ETAD-related work, reference/secondary terminology, footprint handling, and performance improvements | ALUs coherence chain depends heavily on this logic; this is likely one of the highest-risk drift areas |
| Coherence | Current `CoherenceOp` has multiple improvements and defaults changed across Microwave Toolbox versions                                                                     | ALUs `coherence-cuda` should be compared for window defaults, flat-earth phase subtraction, no-data behavior, metadata output, and band selection |
| Range-Doppler terrain correction | Current `RangeDopplerGeocodingOp` has bug fixes and default DEM changes                                                                                                    | ALUs terrain correction and benchmark comparability may be affected by DEM defaults, geolocation fixes, boundary handling, and no-data-at-sea behavior |
| Apply orbit file | Current orbit handling has later bug fixes including recent orbit race-condition work in the wider toolbox history                                                         | ALUs orbit update should be reviewed for benchmark parity, especially when using SNAP-compatible orbit directories |
| Default DEM | Microwave Toolbox release notes show defaulting to Copernicus DEM                                                                                                          | ALUs docs and workflows historically use SRTM3 and later added Copernicus DEM COG support; benchmark definitions must pin DEM explicitly |
| ETAD | Current Microwave Toolbox includes ETAD product reading and ETAD-assisted S1 processing                                                                                    | ALUs does not appear to model ETAD processing; this is likely out of scope unless JRC.D5 benchmarks require ETAD workflows |

**S1C/S1D code evidence**: ALUs parses the SAFE platform metadata as `familyName + number`, producing mission strings such as `SENTINEL-1D` in `sentinel1/s1tbx-io/sentinel1/sentinel1_level1_directory.cc`. Its shared validation then checks the `SENTINEL-1` prefix in `snap-engine/snap-engine-utilities/engine-utilities/gpf/input_product_validator.cc` and `sentinel1/s1tbx-commons/sentinel1_utils.cc`. Current Microwave Toolbox has the same generic `Sentinel1Utils` prefix check, while `sar-op-calibration/.../Sentinel1Calibrator.java` also lists `SENTINEL-1A`, `SENTINEL-1B`, `SENTINEL-1C`, and `SENTINEL-1D` explicitly.

## Sentinel-1 Reader Sync Status

The Sentinel-1 reader section is not fully implemented or fully synced with current Microwave Toolbox. The current ALUs changes are a targeted, IW-relevant subset of SAFE Level-1 reader hardening and geocoding fixes. They should be treated as partial sync work, not as completion of the full `sar-io` reader review.

| Upstream commit | Synced ALUs scope | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `12db283e1` `SNAP-3750 ensure case for CDSE product` | Lower-case image names for image-to-band metadata lookup | Synced |
| `d8cd6bb39` `refactor SafeManifest` | Manifest element lookup accepts both `metadataWrap/xmlData` and direct `xmlData` | Synced subset |
| `73e10e98b` `S1TBX-868 new Spacety format` | Optional `orbitReference`, `OrbitNumber`, `relativeOrbitNumber`, and pass fallback nodes are guarded | Synced subset |
| `d8353246c` `[S1TBX-647] Modified S-1 reader to handle image crossing anti-meridian` | Negative longitudes are normalized before tie-point interpolation when the geolocation grid crosses the antimeridian | Synced, with ALUs runtime warning because this path is not yet validated on ALUs outputs |
| `a8dd51abe` `SNAP-4185 use ProductCache for netcdf readers` | Only the invalid raster/grid dimension guard before tie-point-grid creation was ported | Partial; ProductCache behavior and annotation-only dimension fallback were not ported |
| `f08897475` `fix prefix` | IW-relevant subset: band geocoding is keyed by TOPSAR prefix (`IW1_`, `IW2_`, `IW3_`) instead of concrete band pointer | Partial; WV-specific behavior from surrounding upstream commits is out of scope |
| `4adf88da0` `handle RCM sim RV RH products` | `ImageIOFile::Close()` closes the underlying reader instead of throwing | Synced behavior |
| `057211babf` `S1TBX-758 use min of product dimensions or 10 for the TPG grid`, `904e622ac0` `avoid 1 pixel grid`, `117bd71c68` `S1TBX-895 subsampling as double` | `ReaderUtils::AddGeoCoding()` clamps generated tie-point-grid size and computes subsampling as double; ALUs also fixes the C++ port-specific `CreateFineTiePointGrid()` output-vector pass-by-value bug | Synced; relevant because Range-Doppler can consume product latitude/longitude tie-point grids |

Annotation-only products are not an ALUs target because ALUs is intended to accelerate computations on products with measurement data. The upstream annotation-only dimension fallback associated with `a8dd51abe` is explicitly not implemented. Remaining Sentinel-1 reader review items include updated `sar-io` product-reader behavior, cache/performance changes, full SAFE folder/zip qualification drift, RFI and range-window metadata, and newer product families such as COG/GSLC/ETAD where they affect selected benchmarks. OCN, WV, EW, ETAD, COG, and GSLC support remain out of the current IW-only sync scope unless benchmark inputs require them.

The STEP forum report [Geolocation inaccuracy](https://forum.step.esa.int/t/geolocation-inaccuracy/37504) concerns Range-Doppler terrain correction output shifts that vary with TOPSAR subset size. It is not attributed here to `ReaderUtils::CreateFineTiePointGrid()` alone. However, ALUs `ReaderUtils::CreateFineTiePointGrid()` previously took its output vector by value, making `ReaderUtils::AddGeoCoding()` generate zero-filled product latitude/longitude tie-point grids. Since ALUs Range-Doppler terrain correction can consume product latitude/longitude tie-point grids, this helper is retained in the sync queue and fixed rather than discarded.

## Stepwise Review Plan

| Step | Output |
|---|---|
| 1. Reconstruct per-component lineage | Identify the closest S1TBX-era source state for each ALUs operator/helper using code comments, ALUs git history, function names, behavior, and available SNAP comparison docs |
| 2. Build upstream change inventory | For each operator/helper, list relevant upstream changes from the reconstructed S1TBX-era lineage to current Microwave Toolbox HEAD, excluding pure rename/package changes |
| 3. Classify logical changes | Mark each change as quality-affecting, input-support-affecting, benchmark-default-affecting, performance-only, or not relevant |
| 4. Map to ALUs code | Connect each relevant upstream change to specific ALUs files and functions |
| 5. Define conformance tests | Select minimal S1 datasets and graph parameters to compare latest S1TBX/Microwave Toolbox outputs against ALUs outputs |
| 6. Prepare JRC.D5 review list | Produce a short priority table with effort, risk, expected quality impact, and contract/follow-up recommendation |

## Baseline Reconstruction

The ALUs upstream baseline should be reconstructed per component, not pinned globally. Useful clues already present in the repository are:

| Clue | Value |
|---|---|
| Existing comparison doc | `docs/SNAP_COMPARISON.md` references SNAP engine `8.0.8` and S1TBX `8.0.5` for ALUs `0.6` |
| Later routine docs | Calibration/coherence READMEs compare against SNAP 8 GPT behavior |
| ALUs SAR history | Most core SAR work is from 2020-2023, with 2026 commits mostly build/toolchain refresh |
| Source comments | Many C++ files explicitly name original Java classes and old `senbox-org/s1tbx` paths |

The first formal review action should be to build a per-component lineage table. The lineage does not need to identify one exact upstream commit for every file, but it should identify the closest practical S1TBX-era behavior represented by ALUs before comparing against current Microwave Toolbox logic.

## Benchmark Comparability Notes

Benchmark definitions must pin inputs and processing parameters tightly. Otherwise differences may reflect SNAP default changes rather than ALUs logic drift.

| Parameter | Recommendation |
|---|---|
| SNAP/Microwave Toolbox version | Record exact git commit, not only release label |
| DEM source | Pin SRTM3 or Copernicus DEM explicitly |
| Orbit handling | Pin orbit files or orbit directory contents |
| Input product | Record SAFE product name, IPF version, mission, acquisition mode, product type, polarization, and burst/subswath selection |
| No-data handling | Record output no-data value, valid-pixel mask handling, and statistics exclusion rules |
| Intermediate products | Enable ALUs `--wif` and equivalent SNAP graph outputs for debugging when comparing chains |
| Metrics | Compare geotransform, raster size, no-data mask, valid percentage, min/max/mean/stddev, pixel-wise absolute difference, relative difference, and selected visual diagnostics |
